subject.title: fix(plugins): bound before_tool_call hook with a default timeout

question: Should existing third-party `before_tool_call` handlers be subject to a fixed 15-second default that denies the tool call on expiry, or should the hook contract use a different compatibility policy?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically small, but it changes the runtime outcome of already-installed plugin handlers that take longer than the new default; source inspection alone cannot choose that public plugin-runtime policy.

options.title: Accept the 15-second fail-closed default
options.body: Merge this focused alignment with sibling modifying-hook budgets after adding current-head runtime proof of the terminal timeout classification.

options.title: Choose a different shared budget
options.body: Keep the bounded fail-closed design but set a duration the plugin-hook owner considers safe for legitimate existing handlers.

options.title: Defer the default change
options.body: Leave the current behavior until maintainers define an explicit compatibility and upgrade policy for long-running gating hooks.

recommendation.title: Accept the 15-second fail-closed default
recommendation.body: Merge this focused alignment with sibling modifying-hook budgets after adding current-head runtime proof of the terminal timeout classification.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history identifies this contributor as the only concrete person connected to the current implementation, although a current-main hook owner should make the final policy choice.
